messages:
Maya (Design): quick thread on the tiny-but-mighty controls above the latency heatmap. new proposals: 1) a compact granularity dropdown (1s/10s/1m/auto), 2) a small 'pin metrics' toggle to keep p95/p50 visible while scrolling, and 3) a 'preserve anomalies' checkbox that prevents downsampling of flagged spikes. mock: https://img.redwood.dev/heatmap-controls-v3.png

Rory (Frontend): love the pin idea. question: where does preserve-anomalies live when collapsed? we only have ~48px of header real estate.

Ellen (PM): product use case: on-call engineers need to see spikes even with auto-sampling. preserve-anomalies should be an opt-in on the pill, default off. UX should hint cost implications.

Dev (Eng-Metrics): backend feasibility: we can tag anomaly buckets and force them into the sampled set, but it increases payload. we can return a "costEstimate" when toggling preserve-anomalies for large time ranges.

Kai (a11y): accessibility: granularity dropdown must be keyboard operable and show selected state; pin and preserve toggles must expose aria-pressed and an aria-describedby explaining tradeoffs. announce costEstimate when it changes.

Maya (Design): copy options for the preserve checkbox: "Preserve anomalies (dont downsample spikes)" vs "Preserve anomalies (may increase data cost)". Which is clearer?

Ellen (PM): prefer explicit: include cost hint. maybe use short form in-UI: "Preserve anomalies" and tooltip: "Keeps detected spikes when sampling. May increase load/cost."

Rory (Frontend): implementation note: granular dropdown defaults to auto which adapts sampling based on throughput + time window. need CSS for collapsed small width: show icons only at <420px and full labels otherwise.

Kai (a11y): icons-only mode can be problematic for screen readers. ensure icons have aria-labels and an expanded description reachable via a "More info" link.

Dev (Eng-Metrics): costEstimate API will return estimated bytes and an impact score. client should show a tiny badge: "+X%" when preserve-anomalies is on. we'll throttle estimates to avoid heavy calcs.

Maya (Design): microcopy for badge: "+~12%" with tooltip "estimated increase in data returned". is the tilde ok or should we use exact?

Ellen (PM): tilde is fine, since it's an estimate. also add a confirmation for >50% estimated increase.

Rory (Frontend): keyboard shortcut idea: 'g' to focus granularity, 'p' to toggle pin, 'a' to toggle preserve-anomalies. should be discoverable in the help menu. we'll ensure conflicts are handled.

Kai (a11y): sounds good. when toggles change, use aria-live polite to announce "Preserve anomalies enabled. Estimated data increase: 12 percent." throttle announcements so they don't spam during rapid toggles.

Maya (Design): visual: pin icon when active should be filled and have a tooltip: "Pinned metrics remain visible while you scroll". for collapsed mode we'll show pin + a tiny caret for expand.

Ellen (PM): acceptance criteria: 1) granularity control works with keyboard and mouse; 2) pin keeps metrics visible while scrolling; 3) preserve-anomalies opt-in and shows cost badge and confirmation if >50%; 4) all controls have accessible labels and aria-live announcements; 5) icons-only mode has descriptive aria labels.

Dev (Eng-Metrics): infra tasks: costEstimate endpoint, anomaly-preserve flagging in query engine, rate limits, feature flag rollout. we'll also record analytics events: granularity_change, pin_toggle, preserve_toggle (with cost_estimate bucket).

Rory (Frontend): dev tasks: UI for controls, keyboard shortcuts, aria-live region, tooltip copy, confirmation modal when needed, and analytics hooks. estimate 2 sprints + infra work.

Kai (a11y): i'll draft a checklist including announcement phrasing, focus order, icon alt text, reduced-motion respect, and screen reader walkthrough. will test with VoiceOver + NVDA when prototype is up.

Maya (Design): i'll update the mock to handle narrow widths, include the cost badge, and write the tooltip text. will post Loom with the pin + preserve flows.

ci-bot: CI build queued for branch/heatmap-controls-v3  build#5012 started.

Ellen (PM): thanks team. let's validate with 2 users (on-call SRE and product analyst) during the next usability slot. post the prototype link here when ready.
